events.title: First Successful Telephone Call
events.description: Alexander Graham Bell made the first successful telephone call to his assistant Thomas Watson in Boston, saying, 'Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you.'
events.significance: This moment marked the birth of practical telephony, transforming global communication and laying the foundation for the modern telecommunications industry.

events.title: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo Ratified by U.S. Senate
events.description: The U.S. Senate ratified the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, ending the Mexican-American War. Mexico ceded roughly half of its territory, including present-day California, Nevada, Utah, and parts of other states.
events.significance: The treaty dramatically expanded U.S. territory and reshaped North American geopolitics, with lasting effects on borders, demographics, and the debate over slavery's expansion.

events.title: Tibetan Uprising Begins in Lhasa
events.description: Thousands of Tibetans surrounded the Norbulingka palace to prevent the Dalai Lama from being taken to a Chinese military event, sparking a widespread uprising against Chinese rule.
events.significance: The uprising was suppressed, and the Dalai Lama fled to India, establishing the Tibetan government-in-exile; the date is still commemorated as Tibetan Uprising Day.

events.title: Death of Harriet Tubman
events.description: Harriet Tubman, the abolitionist who escaped slavery and led numerous others to freedom via the Underground Railroad, died in Auburn, New York, at about age 91.
events.significance: Tubman became an enduring symbol of courage and the struggle for freedom and equality, also serving as a Union scout and nurse during the Civil War and later supporting women's suffrage.

events.title: Birth of Lenore Marshall? No: Pacific Cable Era Milestone Replaced by Courrières Mine Disaster
events.description: A massive coal mine explosion at Courrières in northern France killed 1,099 miners, becoming the worst mining disaster in European history.
events.significance: The disaster prompted major labor strikes and reforms in mine safety and workers' rights across France and Europe.
